record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Model theory of deeply/roughly deeply ramified fields, especially F_p((t))^{1/p^infty}
record.original_question: A nontrivially valued field (K, v) is called deeply ramified if it satisfies two conditions: (DRvg) no archimedean component of the value group vK is discrete (i.e., for any two convex subgroups Gamma_1 strictly contained in Gamma_2 of vK, the quotient Gamma_2/Gamma_1 is not isomorphic to Z); and (DRvr) if the residue characteristic char Kv = p > 0, then O_K/pO_K is semiperfect (Frobenius surjective) when char K = 0, and the completion's valuation ring O_{K-hat}/pO_{K-hat} is semiperfect when char K = p. The class of deeply ramified fields contains all perfectoid fields (complete nondiscrete rank-1 valued fields of residue characteristic p with semiperfect O_K/pO_K) and all tame fields. A roughly deeply ramified (rdr) field satisfies (DRvr) together with (DRvp): if char Kv = p > 0, then v(p) is not the smallest positive element of vK. Model-theoretic results analogous to those for tame fields (model completeness relative to value group and residue field) have been established for roughly tame fields (henselian fields satisfying (TF2) Kv perfect, (TF3) algebraically maximal, and the weaker (TF1r): if char Kv = p > 0 the interval [-v(p), v(p)] in vK is p-divisible). What can be said about the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified fields relative to their value groups and residue fields, and in particular what are the model-theoretic properties of F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} (the perfect hull of the formal Laurent series field F_p((t))), which is a deeply ramified field of positive characteristic?

evidence.quote: Open problem 5: What can we say about the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified fields (relative to their value groups and residue fields), and in particular of F_p((t))^{1/p^infty}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let $(K,v)$ be a nontrivially valued field with value group $vK$, valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_K$, residue field $Kv$, and completion $\widehat{K}$.

(a) $(K,v)$ is called deeply ramified if it satisfies:
 (DRvg) no archimedean component of $vK$ is discrete: for any two convex subgroups $\Gamma_1\subsetneq \Gamma_2$ of $vK$, the quotient $\Gamma_2/\Gamma_1$ is not isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}$; and
 (DRvr) if $\operatorname{char} Kv=p>0$, then in case $\operatorname{char} K=0$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_K/p\mathcal{O}_K$ is semiperfect (its Frobenius is surjective), and in case $\operatorname{char} K=p$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_{\widehat{K}}/p\mathcal{O}_{\widehat{K}}$ is semiperfect.

(b) $(K,v)$ is called roughly deeply ramified (rdr) if it satisfies (DRvr) together with:
 (DRvp) if $\operatorname{char} Kv=p>0$, then $v(p)$ is not the smallest positive element of $vK$.

(c) A henselian field $(K,v)$ is called roughly tame if (TF2) $Kv$ is perfect, (TF3) $(K,v)$ is algebraically maximal, and (TF1r) if $\operatorname{char} Kv=p>0$ then the interval $[-v(p),v(p)]\subseteq vK$ is $p$-divisible. Roughly tame fields admit Ax–Kochen/Ershov-type model completeness and relative completeness theorems with respect to $(vK,Kv)$.

Problems.
1. Develop a model theory of deeply ramified fields and of roughly deeply ramified fields, relative to their value groups and residue fields. Specifically, determine whether and under which additional hypotheses an Ax–Kochen/Ershov principle holds for these classes: i.e., whether elementary equivalence (and/or elementary embedding) of two such fields $(K,v)$ and $(L,w)$ in the language of valued fields reduces to elementary equivalence (resp. elementary embedding) of the value groups $vK, wL$ as ordered abelian groups and of the residue fields $Kv, Lw$ as fields.

2. As a particular instance, describe the complete first-order theory of the perfect hull $\mathbb{F}_p((t))^{1/p^{\infty}}$ of the formal Laurent series field $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$, equipped with its natural valuation $v_t$ (which is a deeply ramified field of positive characteristic): identify a natural axiomatization, decide model completeness relative to its value group $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ and residue field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and determine whether $\mathbb{F}_p((t))^{1/p^{\infty}}$ is decidable.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a December 2025 survey on model theory of tame valued fields. Recent work (e.g., AKE principles for deeply ramified fields, and results on perfectoid fields by Jahnke–Kartas) provides partial progress, including AKE principles for certain deeply ramified fields of positive characteristic with fixed degree of imperfection, but a full model-theoretic understanding of (roughly) deeply ramified fields and the decidability/model completeness of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))^{1/p^\infty}$ remain open.
